title: Power Drift
build: Activision original disk, PAL, Securispeed loader (C64 Preservation Project: power_drift[activision_1989](pal).g64)

records.c: The 6510's data direction register for the processor port at $01; no instruction in the game names it.

Text the programmer left in front of the game's first instruction, in PETSCII: two spaces, "pbj gma89", four returns, a colour code, spaces, "POWERDRIFT TM", returns and spaces. Nothing reads it; the loader's JMP $0834 lands just past it.

The game's entry from the loader, and where it comes back after every game: sets up the interrupts (setup_interrupts), the video chip (setup_video) and the random seed (seed_random), resets the sound driver (sound_reset) with $B806 set to 1, runs the course and driver select screen (select_screen), clears the score ($53DC-$53DE), the stage counter $53E5 and the five marks $53F1-$53F5, then resets the sound driver again with $B806 clear and $B804 = 2. Falls into stage_loop.

Sets up one stage and runs it. Builds the stage (setup_stage), resets the draw order of the twelve karts (reset_kart_order), sorts them (sort_karts), draws the panel (draw_panel) and one frame of the view into the back screen, flips the screens, points the raster chain at the race handler (start_race_irqs) and plays the start-lights sequence (start_lights). Then race_frame_loop.

One frame of the race, repeated until the stage ends. Pauses while space is held down (pause_on_space); when bit 5 of $5381 changes, redraws for the change (track_step, scenery_tick, bend_drift); moves the player (move_player), the rivals (move_rivals) and the places (update_place); then builds the next frame in the back screen: where the rivals are on screen (place_rivals), the karts in draw order (sort_karts) and their sprites (copy_kart_sprites), the view cleared (clear_view), the horizon (draw_horizon_rows), the road (draw_road) and the scenery (draw_scenery), waits for the next frame (wait_frame), flips the double buffer $2E and copies the colours (copy_colours). $53CF counts the frames after the finish: when it reaches zero the stage is over. While it is zero and $53AB is still clear, race_clock runs each frame.

The race is over with a place good enough to go on: ends the sound effect playing (sound_end_effect), shows BONUS and 45 minus the seconds of the race time (show_bonus), flashes the big place number at the right of the panel ten times between the sky colour $25 and white, counts the bonus into the score (count_bonus), waits 100 frames, and counts the stage. After the fifth stage of a course it goes to course_complete; otherwise back to stage_loop for the next stage.

The race ended with $53AB set: ends the sound effect playing (sound_end_effect), waits 250 frames, shows GAME OVER (show_game_over), checks the score against the high-score table (high_score_check) and goes back to game_start.
All five stages of the course are done: CONGRATULATIONS across the screen (congratulations), the high-score check (high_score_check), and back to game_start.

Called from $32C3 in the player's update. Every sixteenth call: points the first multiplexed sprite at the chosen driver's forward-facing head ($1779), puts the face last given its second picture back to its first (draw_face_first), and gives a random place from 5th to 12th ($5372 = 4 to 11) its second picture (draw_face_second), so the faces along the panel change expression one at a time.

Inserts the score $53DC-$53DE into the seven-entry table at $0C0F (three BCD bytes each, highest byte first) at the first place it beats, moving the lower entries and their names down one slot, and asks for a name (name_entry). Compares from the bottom entry upward.
Clears the screen to the plain text set (text_screen), writes GAME OVER from $0A56 in the middle of row 12 in colour 9, and waits 250 frames.
"GAME OVER" in the game's alphabet (digits 0-9 at $00-$09, A-N at $0A-$17, O written as zero, P-W at $18-$1F, space $20, X-Z at $21-$23, comma $7D).

Stops CIA 1's timers and turns the sprites off, points the raster chain at $5181 (music only), sets the video chip to screen $EC00 with the character set at $F000, background grey ($0B) and multicolour 2 black, and clears the screen (clear_text_screen).

Asks the player for three letters for the high-score table: NAME ENTRY at the top, a ring of 28 letters (A-Z, comma, end mark $7C) placed around the screen from the offsets at $0BB3. Waits for fire to be let go, then each 5 frames left and right move the highlight round the ring and fire takes the letter under it into $53F7 and shows it at $EDF3; the end mark or a third letter finishes.
"NAME ENTRY" in the game's alphabet.
The 28 letters of the name-entry ring in the game's alphabet: $7C (the end mark), A to Z with O written as zero, and a comma.
Screen offsets (low byte, high byte) of the 28 letters of the name-entry ring, from the top left round the screen.
The high bytes of name_entry_cells, read at its address + 1.

Nine slots of four bytes: the seven names of the high-score table (three letters and a space, in the game's alphabet: CJB, SAD, KOM, OTA, REE, MAT, LCY), then slot 7, which the shuffle in high_score_check writes into, and a ninth nothing uses.
The high-score names from slot 1 on, the address the shuffle in high_score_check writes a name one slot down to.

Nine slots of three BCD bytes, highest first: the seven scores of the table (200000, 190000, 180000, 170000, 150000, 140000, 130000 as shown, with the panel's zero after them), then slot 7, which takes a score that beats none, and a ninth nothing uses.
The middle byte of each high-score slot, read at high_score_scores + 1.
The low byte of each high-score slot, read at high_score_scores + 2.
The high-score slots from slot 1 on, where high_score_check moves a beaten score one slot down.
The middle byte of a high-score slot one down, high_score_check's destination.
The low byte of a high-score slot one down, high_score_check's destination.
Writes the high-score table on the select screen, rows 15 to 21 from column 11: the place 1 to 7 in colour 14, the name (draw_score_name) and the score (draw_score_digits). $5372 counts the rows.
Copies the four bytes of name slot $5372 from high_score_names to the screen at the row pointer $02/$03, offset Y, in colour 8.
Writes the score of slot $5372 from high_score_scores as six digits and a trailing zero, so 020000 reads 0200000, in colour 9.

The course and driver select screen. Points the raster chain at the select handler ($518A), sets the screen to $EC00 with the character set at $F000, grey border and background, multicolour 1 light grey, and clears it. The highlight starts on course C ($53E4 = 2) and the driver cursor on driver 1: $53B7 is set to 0, and driver_cursor_loop moves it on one before it first places the cursor. Draws the five course pictures (draw_course_pictures), the grey bars, the copyright and SELECT COURSE lines, the high-score table and the twelve faces, then runs the cursor until fire. Fire picks the driver under the cursor ($53B7) and the course highlighted ($53E4); then the chosen kart is lowered on its cable (from $0E6A).

For each of the five courses, right to left: a 7 by 7 frame of tiles from $ADDE (stored 256 bytes a row), white round the highlighted course and black round the others; inside it the course's 5 by 5 picture from $9E00 + $0FA6,x in that course's colour from $0FA1; and the course letter A to E below, through the colour buffer at $5590. All drawn with the tile blitter draw_tiles into the back screen, then shown by copy_colours.

Moves sprite 7, the cursor, to the next of the twelve faces every 21 frames ($53B7 wraps 11 to 0), at X = $14E4,driver + 8 doubled, with the ninth bit in $D010. Between moves it watches the stick: fire leaves the loop; every 32nd frame left or right moves the course highlight $53E4 within 0 to 4 and redraws the pictures.

After fire on the select screen: clears to the plain screen, draws the chosen driver's second face at the top centre, and shows the kart as sprites 0 to 3 (positions and pointers from $0FAB, $0FAF, $0FB3) in a random colour from $372E, with the head in sprite 0 in orange. Then every 5 frames: the three columns of rope tiles in rows 0 to 11 are copied one row down, the hook picture from $80B4 (11 by 19 tiles) is drawn with its top at row $0D - 19, and the four sprites move 8 lines with it. $0D starts at $29 and steps by $5372: down by one to $1E, where the step turns to +1 and the head turns to the chosen driver's own ($1779), then up to $2A, where all eight sprites are switched on and the routine returns to start the race.
Screen column of each of the five course pictures on the select screen, minus one for the frame: 1, 9, 17, 25, 33.
Colour-RAM value of each course's picture: $0F, $0D, $0D, $0D, $0A, multicolour cells whose own colour is yellow, green, green, green and red.
Low bytes of each course picture's top-left tile in the sheet at page $9E: $84, $89, $8E, $93, $98, five tiles apart.
X positions of sprites 0 to 3 for the kart on the cable: $AE for the head, then $96, $AE and $C6 for the kart's three parts.
Starting Y positions of sprites 0 to 3 for the kart on the cable: $CC for the head, $E1 for the kart.
Sprite pointers for sprites 0 to 3 on the cable: $44, then $8A, $8B, $8C for the kart; sprite 0 is pointed at $89 straight after.
"COPYRIGHT ACTIVISION,SEGA,CHRIS BUTLER" in the game's alphabet, written on row 24 of the select screen.
"SELECT COURSE AND DRIVER WITH JOYSTICK" in the game's alphabet, row 13 of the select screen.
The last letters of str_select_course, STICK.

Puts back the first picture of the face last given its second (slot $5373 on the panel): the driver in $5374,slot, whose 3 by 3 cells come from face_pointers, drawn at row 0 of the panel screen $E000, column panel_slot_columns,slot, through draw_face_cells.
Draws the second picture (the change of expression) of the face in panel slot $5372, from face2_pointers, and remembers the slot in $5373 so draw_face_first can put it back.
Copies nine screen codes from ($0A) to the 3 by 3 block at ($0E), the offsets from cell_offsets_3x3 (three cells on each of three rows 40 apart). Colours are left as they are.

The end of a course: the plain text screen, then 128 times, every 5 frames, CONGRATULATIONS written at a random place on the screen at $EC00 in a random colour from 1 to 7 (with bit 3 set, so the cells are multicolour). The low byte of the place is below $EE so the word stays in its page; on the last page it can run past the screen's 1,000 cells into the bytes after them. Then waits 250 frames.
" CONGRATULATIONS" in the game's alphabet, 17 bytes with a space at each end, the text congratulations scatters over the screen.

After a stage: writes BONUS over the panel's TIME line (row 3) and puts 45 minus the seconds of the race time, in BCD, into $53EC, shown as two digits in columns 8 and 9 before the line's three zeros. The minutes are not looked at, and a seconds count above 45 wraps: SBC in decimal mode gives $45 - $50 = $95.
"BONUS     000" in the game's alphabet: the 13 cells show_bonus writes at the start of the panel's row 3.

Counts the bonus into the score: once a frame adds 1 to the score's middle BCD byte $53DD (carrying into $53DE), 1,000 points as the panel shows them, redraws the score (draw_score), takes 1 from $53EC and redraws its digits (draw_bonus_digits), until $53EC is zero. draw_score ends with CLD ($34AE), so the subtraction is binary although $53EC holds a BCD number: a bonus shown as 45 counts 69 times, and the digits pass through values such as $3F. The test comes after the subtraction, so a bonus of 0 counts 256 times.

Writes $53EC's two halves as characters at $E080 and $E081, row 3 columns 8 and 9 of the panel. The panel's characters $0A to $0F are the letters A to F, so a half above 9 shows as a hexadecimal digit.

Draws the race panel at the top of the screen at $E000 (rows 0 to 4). The big place number's cells at columns 36 to 38 and its suffix cell get colour 1. The eleven rivals' faces ($53AC lists their drivers) go in row 0 at the columns in panel_rival_columns, recorded in the slot order $5374 by panel_rival_slots, in colour 8; the player's driver $53B7 goes in slot 4, column 12. Rows 3 and 4 come from four 40-byte tables (TIME, STG and the gear's LO on row 3; SCORE, the course, LAP, HI and KM on row 4) with their colours. Then the course letter (draw_course_letter), the marks of the stages done (draw_stage_marks) and the score (draw_score), and blanks at $E027 and $E04F.
Row 3 of the race panel, 40 cells in the game's alphabet: TIME 0'00'00 (the apostrophes are $49), STG and five stage boxes ($40 to $44) at columns 25 to 29, and $45 L O at columns 31 to 33.
Colour RAM values for the 40 cells of panel_row3_text.

Row 4 of the race panel: SCORE 0000000, four course cells at columns 15 to 18 (draw_course_letter rewrites them), LAP and four lap boxes ($40 to $43) at columns 25 to 28, $46 H I at columns 31 to 33, and 000KM at columns 35 to 39.
Colour RAM values for the 40 cells of panel_row4_text.
Column in row 0 of each rival's face at the start of a stage: 0, 3, 6, 9, then 15 to 33 in steps of 3, leaving column 12, the fifth place, for the player.
The place slot (0 to 11) of each of the eleven rivals at the start of a stage: 0 to 3, then 5 to 11, so the player starts in slot 4, fifth.
Addresses of the twelve drivers' faces, 9 screen codes each (3 by 3 cells), the picture the panel and the select screen normally show. The faces follow from $129D.
The high bytes of face_pointers, read at its address + 1.
The twelve drivers' faces for the panel and the select screen, 3 by 3 cells each, nine bytes a face, in the panel's character set at $F000.
Addresses of the twelve drivers' second faces, the change of expression shown for a moment on the panel and when the kart is lowered on the select screen. The faces follow from $1321.
The high bytes of face2_pointers, read at its address + 1.
The twelve drivers' second faces, 3 by 3 cells each, nine bytes a face.
For each of the five stages with a mark in $53F1-$53F5 (non-zero), writes cell $C1 in the stage box at row 3, columns 25 to 29, in the mark's colour.
Writes the four cells of course $53E4 (A to E) into row 4, columns 15 to 18, from course_letter_cells, with colours from course_letter_colours.
Four cells for each course, stored right to left: the letter A to E (shown in column 18) and three cells of the strip before it.
Colour RAM values for course_letter_cells, four for each course.

Once a race frame until the player finishes ($53CF set): works out the player's place. The rivals keep their order (rival 0 is the fastest), so it looks from rival 10 upward for the first one ahead of the player, by laps ($53B8,x against $53A7), then the coarse position ($5382,x against $5380, a negative one counting as behind) and the fine one ($538E,x against $5381). The place is that rival's number plus one (0 is first). When it differs from $53D6 it starts sound effect 2 ($B805) and calls show_place.

Shows place X (0 to 11) on the panel: the suffix cell at $E077 (st, nd, rd or th, from place_suffix), sprite 7's position over the faces ($53EB from slot_marker_x), the big number at columns 36 to 38 (its source address is written into the LDA at $145B), and swaps the faces in the new and old slots, with the slot order $5374. When the player has moved up, the player's own face shows its second picture and the kart's head sprite turns to look back ($1785); when the player has dropped, the face of the driver now in the player's old slot shows its second picture. Clears $53F6, the counter of panel_faces_tick. Also called once at the start of a stage (from $36C8).
The low byte of the address in the LDA at $145B, which show_place sets to the place's big number.
The high byte of the address in the LDA at $145B, set by show_place with the low byte.
Addresses of the big place numbers 1 to 12, 3 by 3 cells each, the data from $14F0.
The high bytes of place_number_pointers, read at its address + 1.
Column in row 0 of each of the twelve place slots on the panel, 3 apart: 0 to 33.
The suffix cell after the big place number, at $E077: $24 st, $25 nd, $26 rd, then $27 th for places 4 to 12.
Offsets of the nine cells of a 3 by 3 block on a 40-column screen: 0, 1, 2, 40, 41, 42, 80, 81, 82.
Sprite 7's X position, halved, over each of the twelve faces: $0C to $90 in steps of $0C. Used for the cursor on the select screen and for the marker over the player's face in the race.
The big numbers 1 to 12 drawn at the right of the panel, 3 by 3 cells each, nine bytes a number, spaces ($20) where a number is narrower.

After the kart has fallen off a raised stretch of track (called from $3346): calls hide_rival_sprites, copies and sorts the kart sprites, sets the kart straight, then eight times, two frames apart, clears the back screen, draws wipe wedge 0 to 7 into it (wipe_wedge) and flips the screens, with the horizon's colour change set early ($24 = $15); waits 50 frames, puts the road back under the middle of the kart ($2F = $E0), draws the view afresh with the road and scenery, and starts the kart dropping from the top of the view: $53E9 set, the head sprite's Y at $64, the speed at 2 ($53D5), $536F = 10, the speed read-out at 70 ($53DA/$53DB) and the frame counter $E5 reset.

While $53E9 is set, once a frame from the race's top-of-screen interrupt: the kart drops. The fall speed $53D5 grows by one every other frame and is added to the head sprite's Y ($5151); the kart's three sprites sit 21 lines below it. At line $E1 the drop ends ($53E9 cleared).

Draws wedge X (0 to 6; 7 draws nothing) into the back screen and straight into colour RAM: for $166B+1 rows from the row and column given by wipe_rows_lo, wipe_rows_hi and wipe_columns, a first cell from wipe_first_char then cell 6 out to the edge of the screen in the direction wipe_direction, all in the sky colour $25; each row starts wipe_slope columns over from the one above.
Low byte of the screen offset of each wipe wedge's top row ($C8 is row 5, the top of the view); 0 at index 7 ends the wipe.
High byte of the screen offset of each wipe wedge's top row.
Starting column of each wipe wedge.
Rows of each wipe wedge, less one.
The screen code of each wedge row's first cell; the rest of the row is cell 6.
Column step along each wedge row: +1 fills to the right edge, -1 ($FF) to the left.
Column step from each wedge row to the next: +1, 0 or -1.

The player's update while the kart spins out (called from $329C): starts sound effect 3. While the spin counter $53D1 is above 1 it steps the spin frame $53E3 (0 to 7) every other race frame and takes 1 from $53D1 every eighth; the kart's sprites take that frame's pointers and the head's X from spin_kart_1 to spin_head_x, and the head the picture from the table spin_head_tables names for the frame. The road slides back one step a frame until the kart is in its middle ($2F towards $E0), the horizon scrolls by $53D1 columns ($53A8, 0 to 39), and $53D2 grows by $53D1, wrapping from $50 to $D6 + $53D1; while it is from 0 to $31, $53D3 = 4 x $53D2 + 10. Once the spin has slowed to 1 and $53D2 reaches $14, the spin ends (reset_kart_height), $53D0 is cleared, $EE and $AA are written to $F0BE and $F0BF (the last two lines of character $17 of the panel set, which hold those values already) and the sound effect is ended (sound_end_effect). Otherwise on to j_337C.
Sprite 1's pointer for each of the eight spin frames.
Sprite 2's pointer for each of the eight spin frames.
Sprite 3's pointer for each of the eight spin frames.
The head sprite's X position for each of the eight spin frames.
For each of the eight spin frames, the table of head pictures by driver: head_behind for frames 0 to 2, head_front for 3 to 7.
The high bytes of spin_head_tables, read at its address + 1.
Sprite pointer of each driver's head seen from behind, as the player sees their own kart in the race. Several drivers share $44 and $70.
Sprite pointer of each driver's head turned to look back, shown when the player overtakes.
Sprite pointer of each driver's head seen from the front, $8D to $98, for the kart turned round in a spin and for the finishers stacked on the podium.

The start of a stage. Fills bands 3 and 2 of the sprite table at $513D, every fourth byte from $5140 and $513F, from start_band3 and start_band2: band 3 is four red sprites side by side at line $5A, the START sign; band 2 is the three lights at line $82, light red, orange and green, dim. After 100 frames the first light turns red ($5173 = 2) and the second yellow ($5177 = 7); after 100 more the second goes back to orange and the third turns light green ($517B = $0D); 50 frames later both bands are switched off again from start_band3_off and start_band2_off, and the race begins.
The 17 values of band 3 of the sprite table for the start: on, X $8A, $A2, $BA, $D2, Y $5A for all four, pointers $69 to $6C, colour 2 (red) for all four. Written one every fourth byte from $5140.

The 17 values of band 2 for the start: on, X $50, $68, $80 (sprite 3 at 0), Y $82, pointers $6D, $6E, $6F (and $49), colours $0A, 8 and 5, the three lights unlit. Written one every fourth byte from $513F.
Band 3's values after the start: off, with a kart's positions, pointers and colours in place for a finisher.
Band 2's values after the start: off, with a kart's positions, pointers and colours in place for a finisher.

Copies the two horizon pictures into the back screen, 40 cells of each row from column $53A8 (so the horizon scrolls sideways as the track turns): the lower picture, from the address at $53ED/$53EE, up to three rows with its bottom row on screen row $53A9 (left out when $53A9 is 22 or more); then the upper one, from $53EF/$53F0, up to four rows with its bottom row on row $53A9 - 6. Neither goes above row 5, the view's first. The source and destination addresses are written into the LDA and STA of the copy loops at $1877 and $18D0.
The low byte of the LDA's address at $1877, the lower horizon picture's row, written by draw_horizon_rows.
The high byte of the LDA's address at $1877, stepped down a page for each row copied.
The low byte of the STA's address at $187A, the screen row the lower horizon row goes to.
The high byte of the STA's address at $187A, the back screen's page.
The low byte of the LDA's address at $18D0, the upper horizon picture's row, written by draw_horizon_rows.
The high byte of the LDA's address at $18D0, stepped down a page for each row copied.
The low byte of the STA's address at $18D3, the screen row the upper horizon row goes to.
The high byte of the STA's address at $18D3, the back screen's page.

Copies the twelve sprite records the rivals are drawn with (X halved $4A, Y $5A, pointer $6A, colour $7A) to the copies the raster interrupt reads ($8A, $9A, $AA, $BA), so the interrupt does not read records place_rivals is still building. The draw order $CA-$D5 has no copy: the interrupt reads it where sort_karts reorders it, just before this. A near rival takes up to four records, a distant one one.

Sorts the draw order $CA-$D5 of the twelve sprite records by their Y position $5A, largest first, with passes up and down the list (a cocktail sort) until a pass swaps nothing. The interrupt places the last four of the list, the records highest on the screen, first.
Sets the draw order $CA-$D5 to 0 to 11.

Once a race frame: each rival's speed $E7,x creeps up by 1 every other frame to its top speed in rival_top_speeds, and is added to its fine position $538E,x with the carry into $5382,x. A coarse position of 50 ($32) is a lap: $53B8,x counts it and the position starts again at 0. At the fourth lap the rival has finished (place_finisher).
Top speed of each of the eleven rivals: $1E for rival 0 down to $0C for rival 10.

A rival (X) has finished. While podium places are left ($53AA, 3 at the start), puts the rival on the podium: band $53AA of the sprite table at $513D is switched on, its kart takes the rival's colour ($53C3,x), its head the rival's face from the front ($8D plus the driver number), and the place label for that band (podium_labels) is copied into the top five lines of that face's sprite in the video bank at $C000. When the last place goes, $53AB is set: the game is over.

Three sprite pictures five lines high, 3 bytes a line: "3rd", "2nd" and "1st", copied into the top of a podium face. The first finisher takes 1st (podium band 3, at the top), the second 2nd, the third 3rd.
Fills the colour buffer $5400-$57FF with 8 and the screen $EC00-$EFFF with spaces ($20).

Points the player's kart sprites at steering frame $53E2 (0 hard left, 2 straight, 4 hard right): the head's X from kart_head_x and the first body sprite from kart_body_frames, the second and third the next two pointers. Every eight frames the body switches to a second set of pointers (index + 5), which differs from the first for every frame but the straight one.
Sprite 1's pointer for steering frames 0 to 4, then the second set used every other eight frames.
The head sprite's X position for steering frames 0 to 4.

Called when the track position moves on a step: each of the four scenery slots $31-$34 counts down, and a slot that runs out takes the next scenery record (next_scenery_record) and starts again from 15.

Reloads slot X's counter with 15 and makes it the newest slot ($42), then reads the next three-byte scenery record from the stream ($46) at $48 into $35,x, $3D,x and $39,x. After four records (offset 12) the stream moves to the next entry of the stage's list (scenery_list_next).
The entry of next_scenery_record that leaves the slot's counter alone: reads the next three-byte record for slot X. setup_stage calls it for the four slots at the start.

Reads the entry at offset $49 of the stage's list at ($E3), two bytes each. An address below $4000 is the next scenery stream: it goes in $46/$47 and the stream starts at offset 0. $FF in the high byte starts the list again from 0. Any other address is a block of character pictures: 1,400 bytes ($578) from it are copied to $FA10-$FF87, characters $42 to $FF of the race's character set at $F800, and the list moves on to its next entry.

Course A, stage 1: the scenery list scenery_list_next reads, 28 two-byte entries and $FFFF: 25 scenery streams, four records each, and the character blocks $5D98, $6888 and $6310 copied in at their places in the list; it starts with the stream at $22F9.

Course A, stage 2: the scenery list scenery_list_next reads, 28 two-byte entries and $FFFF: 25 scenery streams, four records each, and the character blocks $6888, $5D98 and $6310 copied in at their places in the list; it starts with the stream at $22F9.

Course A, stage 3: the scenery list scenery_list_next reads, 31 two-byte entries and $FFFF: 25 scenery streams, four records each, and the character blocks $6888, $5D98, $6888, $5D98, $6888 and $6310 copied in at their places in the list; it starts with the stream at $22F9.

Course A, stage 4: the scenery list scenery_list_next reads, 29 two-byte entries and $FFFF: 25 scenery streams, four records each, and the character blocks $5D98, $6310, $5D98 and $6310 copied in at their places in the list; it starts with the stream at $22F9.

Course A, stage 5: the scenery list scenery_list_next reads, 27 two-byte entries and $FFFF: 25 scenery streams, four records each, and the character blocks $5D98 and $6310 copied in at their places in the list; it starts with the stream at $22F9.

Course B, stage 1: the scenery list scenery_list_next reads, 29 two-byte entries and $FFFF: 25 scenery streams, four records each, and the character blocks $6888, $5D98, $6888 and $6310 copied in at their places in the list; it starts with the stream at $22F9. After the last block comes one more stream, $21A9.

Course B, stage 2: the scenery list scenery_list_next reads, 29 two-byte entries and $FFFF: 25 scenery streams, four records each, and the character blocks $6888, $6310, $5820 and $6310 copied in at their places in the list; it starts with the stream at $22F9. The player's kart, once a race frame. After the finish ($53CF set) it does nothing; a spin hands over to kart_spin, and while the kart is dropped back onto the track ($53E9) it goes straight to move_on. In a jump ($53E8) it only sets the heights of the head and kart from jump_head_y, then the kart's picture and the road's sideways slide $30, which keeps the value it had at the take-off, and moves on: the stick does nothing in the air. Otherwise: the panel's faces (panel_faces_tick); when moving, left on the stick slides the road +3 a race frame and turns the kart one frame towards hard left every fourth race frame, right -3 and towards hard right; with neither the kart turns back towards straight every other frame. The road's offset $2F stays within $A8 to $1B. The kart is on the road while $2F is from $C0 to $FF. Off it, on a raised stretch ($53D4) it falls (drop_kart_back); then, there as anywhere off the road, above speed level 3 it slows down. Up accelerates (speed_up) every other race frame, to level 18 in low gear and 32 in high gear, where below level 14 it gains only one race frame in four; otherwise the kart slows every other frame (slow_down), twice when down is held. Then the kart moves on by its speed, laps and finishes, the score (add_speed_score) and the gear change on fire.

Adds the speed level $536F to the position $5380/$5381; 50 coarse steps are a lap ($53A7). After the fourth lap the race is over for the player: $53CF = 60 race frames to the end; rival 10 takes the kart's lane, position 0, speed and colour, so the kart drives on up the road as a rival while the view stays; band 0's sprites point at $89; and the player goes onto the podium as finisher 11 (place_finisher), with the stage's box ($53F1 + stage) marked in the colour of the place taken (podium_colours). Before that, each lap colours the lap boxes on row 4: the one for the lap done red, the next white.

Fire changes gear, once a press ($53D8 holds it until fire is let go): $53D9 0 is low, 1 high. The arrows in column 31 of rows 3 and 4 and the colours of LO and HI follow, from gear_arrow_lo, gear_arrow_hi, gear_colour_lo and gear_colour_hi.

The colour of a stage's mark by the podium places left after the player's finish: $0A for third, $0B for second, $0F for first.
Adds a quarter of the speed level (0 to 8) to the score $53DC-$53DE in decimal mode, each race frame, and falls into draw_score.
Writes the score's six BCD digits from $53DE down into row 4, columns 6 to 11 ($E0A6-$E0AB); column 12 stays the zero after them.

Every other race frame: adds one to the digit after the seconds, $53E1 (shown at $E083), which runs 0 to 5; the sixth carries a second into $53E0 (BCD, shown at $E080 and $E081), and 60 seconds a minute into $53DF ($E07E). The clock runs on race frames, not on the video's 50 a second.
If the speed level $536F is below 32: one level up, and 7 more on the km/h read-out $53DA/$53DB (BCD), shown at $E0C3-$E0C5.
If the speed level is above 0: one level down and 7 off the km/h read-out.

Pauses the race while CIA 1's port B reads $EF (bit 4 low, the space bar): waits for it to be let go, pressed again, and let go again, a frame at a time.

The tile blitter: copies a picture of $12 by $13 cells from ($0A), whose rows are 256 bytes apart, into the back screen with its bottom row at row $0D and its left at column $0C, in colour $14 through the colour buffer at $5400. A zero cell is left out, so the picture is cut round its shape. Cut at the left and right edges of the screen and at the bottom of the colour buffer; rows from -25 to 24 are allowed, so a picture can hang off the top.
High byte of the screen being drawn into, by $2E: $E8 (the screen at $E800) or $EC.
High byte of row x 40 for rows -25 to 25, added to the screen's page, and to $54 for the colour buffer.
Low byte of row x 40 for rows -25 to 25.
An RTS, where draw_road ends when a row has no width left or reaches the jump's gap (from $458B and $459B).

Draws the road into the back screen a row at a time from row 24 upward. Row r (from 0 at the bottom) is left out below $53E6 and the road stops at $53E7 (a jump's gap) or at a zero width in the width list ($1E); a width of $80 is a row hidden behind a crest. The left edge is the road's position $53D2, plus the bend's offset for the row ($27), plus the road's offset $2F times the row's width times four, over 256; the right edge is the left plus the width, both cut to the screen. Between them it writes the road cell $01, then the left and right edges (road_left_edge, road_right_edge) from how far each has moved since the row below.
The flat road's width in cells for each row from the bottom: $22 (34) narrowing by four a row to 2, then 0, the end: nine rows.
The screen row of each of the 16 scenery distances on flat road: 24 for the nearest up to 16.
The sprite Y of a rival at each of the 32 distances on flat road: $E1 for the nearest up to $9D.

The width, scenery-row and kart-height lists of the hills, which the piece routines' tables point into, from here to $4E23: width lists end with 0 and use $80 for a row hidden behind a crest; kart heights of 0 hide a rival.
The road's width, scenery-row and kart-height lists for the hills, continued from road_profiles to $4E23.

Draws the road's left edge on this row: how far the edge has moved since the row below ($15 - $17, or 0 after a hidden row), plus 3 and kept from 0 to 9, picks one of ten routines from left_edge_routines. Routines 3 to 9 write one to five cells leftward from the column before the road; 0 to 2, for an edge moving out, write over the road's first cells. Some choose their cell from the fraction of the offset ($1C).
The ten left-edge routines, by the edge's movement plus 3.
The high bytes of left_edge_routines, read at its address + 1.
An upright left edge: cell $29, $28 or $27 by the fraction $1C (below $40, below $C2, above).
The left edge one column in: cell $26 or $21 by the fraction $1C.
The left edge two columns in: cells $23 and $22.
The left edge three columns in (also for four): cells $23, $24 and $22.
The left edge five columns in: cells $2A, $24 and $25 twice.
The left edge six or more columns in: cells $2A twice, $24 and $25 twice.
The left edge one column out: cell $1F or $1E by the fraction $1C, on the road's first cell.
The left edge two columns out: cells $1C and $1D over the road's first two cells.
The left edge three or more columns out: cells $1C, $0F and $1D over the road's first three cells.

Draws the road's right edge on this row, as road_left_edge does on the left: the movement $18 - $16 plus 3, kept from 0 to 9, picks one of right_edge_routines, which write rightward from column $16, stopping at column 40.
The ten right-edge routines, by the edge's movement plus 3.
The high bytes of right_edge_routines, read at its address + 1.
An upright right edge: cell $16, $17 or $18 by the fraction $1C.
The right edge one column in: cell $1B or $14 by the fraction $1C.
The right edge two columns in: cells $19 and $1A.
The right edge three columns in (also for four): cells $19, $15 and $1A.
The right edge five columns in: cells $2A, $15 and $25 twice.
The right edge six or more columns in: cells $2A twice, $15 and $25 twice.
The right edge one column out: cell $10 or $11 by the fraction $1C, on the road's last cell.
The right edge two columns out: cells $13 and $12 over the road's last two cells.
The right edge three or more columns out: cells $13, $0E and $12 over the road's last three cells.
Waits for the frame counter $E5 to change. The raster interrupt at the top of the screen adds one to it: the race's at $51DF and the select screen's at $518A.

Points the raster chain at race_irq_top, stops CIA 1's and CIA 2's timers and turns off CIA 1's interrupts, banks out the KERNAL ($01 bit 1 cleared, so $01 = $35), points the NMI vector at a lone RTI ($507E) and the IRQ vector at irq_handler, and sets the video chip's interrupt mask to $F0, no source enabled.
Points the raster chain at race_irq_top and falls into enable_raster.
Turns on the raster interrupt (mask $F1) at line $2F and CIA 1's interrupts from timers A and B ($83 to $DC0D).
The NMI handler: a lone RTI, so RESTORE does nothing.

Every interrupt comes here. A raster interrupt is acknowledged and jumps through the pointer at $08/$09 with interrupts enabled again, so the handlers form a chain, each setting the next line and the next handler. A CIA 1 timer A interrupt, after eight NOPs, sets the background colour to $26: the change from sky to ground at the horizon. Otherwise it was timer B: sprite_band_irq.

CIA 1 timer B: places sprites 0 to 3 for band $E0 of sprite_bands (X, Y, colour and pointer for each, the pointer written into all three screens' pointer bytes). A band whose flag is clear is skipped back to band 0, the player's kart. While $E0 counts down from 3 to 0 the timer is restarted for $0900 cycles, about 36 lines, so the bands go down the screen.

Four bands of four sprites each, reused down the screen by sprite_band_irq: band 0 (index 0 of each field) is the player's kart at the bottom, bands 1 to 3 the finishers on the podium and, at the start, the lights and the START sign. Fields of four bytes, one per band: on flags at $513D, then each sprite's X ($5141 sprite 0, $5145, $5149, $514D), Y ($5151 to $515D), pointer ($5161 to $516D) and colour ($5171 to $517D). Band 0 is always on.
Band 1's on flag, the first podium place, which setup_stage clears with bands 2 and 3.
Band 2's on flag; start_lights writes band 2's values from here, one every fourth byte.
Band 3's on flag; start_lights writes band 3's values from here, one every fourth byte.
Sprite 0's X in bands 0 to 3. Sprite 0 is the driver's head.
Sprite 1's X in bands 0 to 3, the left of the kart.
Sprite 2's X in bands 0 to 3, the middle of the kart.
Sprite 3's X in bands 0 to 3, the right of the kart.

Sprite 1's Y in bands 0 to 3.

Sprite 1's pointer in bands 0 to 3.
Sprite 2's pointer in bands 0 to 3.

The raster handler of the text screens: plays the sound (sound_play) and returns, leaving the raster line where it was.

The select screen's handler at line $5A: multicolour 2 light blue ($0E) from there down, and back to select_irq_top at line 0.

The race's first raster handler, at the top of the frame: starts timer B for $1400 cycles to place the first sprite band, sets $E0 = 3, adds one to the frame counter $E5, sets the sky colour $25 as the background, multicolours $0F and 8, and the panel's screen $E000 with the character set at $F000 ($D018 = $8C). Starts timer A for $24 x 256 cycles, the line where the sky turns to ground. Then the kart's drop (drop_kart_step) while $53E9 is set, a flash of the current stage's box every 16 frames, sprite 7 (pointer $83) at line $2E over the player's face ($53EB), and the sound (sound_play). Next: panel_irq_lower at line $4A.
At line $4A, the panel's rows 3 and 4: multicolour 2 black, and race_irq_view at line $5A.

At line $5A, the top of the view: the screen the game is not drawing into ($D018 from view_d018 by $2E), multicolour 1 from $53EA, multicolour 2 black. Places the four karts highest on the screen (the last four of the draw order $CA) in sprites 4 to 7, then hands over to kart_mux_irq, at a line set from kart slot 7's Y.
Sets the next raster interrupt seven lines above the next kart's Y, unless the beam is already past it, then the kart is placed at once.
JMP $5344, which nothing reaches: the handler address stored at $52CE is $52FA, just after it.

The kart multiplexer: takes the next kart in the draw order (slot $DC, going down the list), and once the hardware sprite $DB it is to reuse is 20 lines above the beam, gives it that kart's Y, X (doubled, with the ninth bit), pointer and colour. Sprites 4 to 7 are reused in turn. After the last kart: raster line 0 and race_irq_top.
AND masks clearing one bit of $D010 for sprites 0 to 7; the multiplexer uses those of sprites 4 to 7, from $5363.
The AND masks for sprites 4 to 7 the multiplexer indexes from here.
OR bits setting one bit of $D010 for sprites 0 to 7; the multiplexer uses those of sprites 4 to 7, from $536B.
The OR bits for sprites 4 to 7 the multiplexer indexes from here.

The sound driver's entry once a frame, from the race's top-of-screen interrupt and the text screens': JMP to sound_frame.
An RTS between the entry and the driver's switches.
The tune sound_reset starts: 1 on the name entry, 2 for the race; 0 is silence.

Written by the game to start a sound effect on voice 3: 2 when the place changes or a rival is alongside, 3 for a spin. sound_frame starts it and clears it. Effects 1 and 4 are stored but nothing in the game writes them here.
While not zero the music is not played, only the effects: game_start sets it for the select screen and clears it for the race.
While not zero no new effect starts. Nothing writes it, so it stays 0.
Set when effect 4 starts; while set, the end of any other effect starts effect 4 again (sound_end_effect). Only the routine at $C01C clears it, and nothing calls that.
A NOP byte after the switches.

Silences the chip (sound_silence), clears the driver's workspace (sound_clear_voices, sound_clear_registers), sets the volume from $C237 ($0F, full), points the three voices at the silent pattern (sound_silent_patterns), starts tune $B804 (sound_start_tune), and gates every voice off.

One frame of sound. Starts a new effect when $B805 holds one: its pattern from effect_table, effect 4 also setting $B808, and voice 3's effect state cleared. Then sound_voices, and $C0BA = the raster line when it ended.
Two bytes between sound_frame and sound_voices that nothing reads.

Steps each voice with sound_voice_step: the three music voices (unless $B806 is set), each with its state copied into $FA-$FF and back, its shadow registers at $C0BE, $C0C5 and $C0CC, its workspace at $C055, $C06D and $C085, and its control register's offset in $C0B9 (4, $0B, $12). While an effect plays ($C0BB), voice 3's gate-offs go to the spare buffer at $C0EC instead of the chip, and the effect is stepped as a fourth voice with its shadow registers at $C0E3. Then writes the shadow registers to the SID, voice 3 from the effect's when one plays.

One voice for one frame. While its note's length ($F8 + 0 and + 1) has not run out: one less, the next step of its wave table (sound_wave_step), and its slides (from $BC28). When it runs out, read the next pattern bytes (sound_read_pattern).
An RTS after sound_voice_step's JMP to sound_slides that nothing reaches.

Reads the voice's pattern at ($FE). $FE introduces a command, its number an offset into the jump table at $BBFB. Otherwise the gate is turned off and the byte is a note: 0 a rest (the silent wave $C231), else the note's frequency from note_frequencies, the wave table from the voice's instrument ($F8 + $0A), and its vibrato restarted (+$13 from +$14, +$11 from +$12, +$10 = $99 when on). The next byte is the length: an index into the tune's length table (whose address sound_start_tune writes into both LDAs, at $BBBD and $BBC4, the second reading with X one higher), or 0 and a two-byte length after it. Then the first step of the wave table.
The low byte of the length table's address in the LDA at $BBBD, written by sound_start_tune.
The high byte of the length table's address in the LDA at $BBBD.
The low byte of the same address in the LDA at $BBC4, which reads each length's high byte.
The high byte of the same address in the LDA at $BBC4.
A pattern command: adds the byte after $FE to $BBFB and jumps there through the JMP at $BBF8, whose address it rewrites.
The low byte of the JMP at $BBF8, $FB plus the command's number.
The high byte of the JMP at $BBF8.

The commands' jump table, three bytes apiece, indexed by the command's number: 0 is three BRKs; 3 next pattern, 6 set registers, 9 slide, 12 slide off, 15 vibrato, 18 vibrato off, 21 pulse sweep, 24 pulse sweep off, 27 instrument, 30 end of effect, 33 set effect registers, 36 effect release, 39 go to, 42 tone. 18, 24 and 33 appear in no tune or effect; 36 only in effect 1 and 42 only in effect 4, which nothing starts.

The JMPs of commands 3 to 42, one a command, three bytes apart: cmd_next_pattern, cmd_set_registers, cmd_slide, cmd_slide_off, cmd_vibrato, cmd_vibrato_off, cmd_pulse_sweep, cmd_pulse_sweep_off, cmd_instrument, sound_end_effect, cmd_set_effect_registers, cmd_effect_release, cmd_goto and cmd_tone.

A voice's continuous changes, once a frame: the pulse sweep (+$17: 1 up, 2 down, by +$16, turning at $0F00 and at 0), the frequency slide (+$0C: 1 up, 2 down, by +$0D, to the target at +$0E/+$0F, where it stops) and, with no slide, the vibrato: after the delay +$11, every +$14 + 1 frames the bit pattern +$10 ($99 at each note) is rotated a place, and its low bit lowers the frequency by +$15 or raises it.

Command 3, the end of a pattern: takes the next pattern address from the voice's order list at ($FA). $FE then 0 in the list starts it again from its loop point (+8 and +9 of the workspace), $FE then another byte makes that byte the pattern's high byte.
Command 6: pairs of an index and a value into the shadow registers from $C0BE, until $FF.
Command 33: pairs of an index and a value into the bytes from $C0D5, until $FF; then on as command 6. No pattern that plays uses it.

Command 39: the pattern goes on at the address in the next two bytes. Effects 3 and 4 loop with it: effect 3 back to its last note, which sounds until kart_spin ends the effect (sound_end_effect from $16B1), effect 4 for ever.
Command 9: four bytes into +$0C to +$0F of the workspace: the slide's direction, its step, and the frequency it stops at.
Command 12: the slide off (+$0C = 0).
Command 42: gate off, the frequency from the next two bytes straight into the effect's shadow registers ($C0E3/$C0E4), then on as a note with its length. Only effect 4 uses it.
Command 15: three bytes, the delay at each note's start (+$12), the frames between steps (+$14) and the step (+$15), and +$10 = $99, vibrato on.
Command 18: the vibrato off (+$10 = 0). No pattern that plays uses it.
Command 21: the pulse sweep's step into +$16, and +$17 = 1, sweeping up.
Command 24: the pulse sweep off (+$17 = 0). No pattern that plays uses it.
Command 27: the next two bytes, the address of a wave table, become the voice's instrument (+$0A/+$0B).

Ends the effect playing: $C0BB and $B805 cleared and voice 3's sustain and release set to 0; if $B808 is set, effect 4 starts again. Command 30 ends every effect's pattern here, and the game calls it when a race ends and after a spin.

Command 36: reads $DC01 and ignores it, ORs the next byte into the effect's sustain and release ($C0E9), sets the effect's length ($C09D/$C09E) from the next two, and turns the gate off. No pattern that plays uses it.
Writes 0 to the SID's 28 registers $D400-$D41B.
Clears the three music voices' workspaces, $C055-$C09C.
Clears the music voices' shadow registers, $C0BE-$C0D2.
Starts tune $B804 from tune_table: the three voices' order lists into $C05D, $C075 and $C08D, and the tune's length table's address into the two LDAs at $BBBD and $BBC4.

The next step of the voice's wave table at ($FC): two bytes, the sustain and release and the control register (waveform and gate), until $FF, where the table stays. While an effect plays the volume is set to $0F again each step.
LDA #0, STA $B808, STA $B805, JSR $BF17: switches the engine-like effect 4 off for good. Nothing calls it.
Points the three voices' patterns at $C0B5 and their order lists at $C0B7, a pattern that ends at once and a list that loops on itself, so a voice with no tune is silent.
$FE $03: a pattern that is only the command to take the next one.
$FE $00: an order list that only says to start again from the voice's loop point, which sound_start_tune has set to the tune's own list.
Tune 2's note lengths in frames, two bytes each, by index: 0 (explicit), 3, 7, 11 and on in steps of four.
Tune 1's note lengths in frames, two bytes each, by index: 0 (explicit), 5, 11, 17 and on in steps of six.
The SID frequency of each note number, two bytes each: 0 for a rest, then $0314 upward, a semitone apart.
The wave table of a rest: sustain and release 0, control $11 (triangle, gate on) with nothing to sound, then $FF.
The volume, $0F, which sound_reset writes to $D418, and its pair; then the patterns of effects 1 to 4: $C324, $C346, $C363, $C37C.
The instruments: lists of steps of two bytes, sustain and release then waveform and gate, each ended by $FF, one step a frame (noise $81, triangle $11, pulse $41, sawtooth $21), to $C323.
Effect 1's pattern. Nothing in the game starts it.
Effect 2's pattern: a place won or lost, or a rival alongside.
Effect 3's pattern: the spin. It ends with command 39 back to its last note, so the note holds until kart_spin ends the effect.
Effect 4's pattern: a steady tone at $0BB8 with a sweeping pulse, which loops with command 39 until another effect stops it, an engine's hum. Nothing in the game starts it.
More instruments, steps of two bytes ended by $FF, to $C4B9.
Eight bytes a tune: the order lists of voices 1, 2 and 3 and the length table. Tune 0 is all zeros; tune 1, the name entry's, from $C4C2; tune 2, the race's, from $C4CA.
Tune 1's order lists: the pattern addresses of voice 1 from $C4D2, voice 2 from $C4E4, voice 3 from $C4EE, each ended by $FE $00 to loop.
Tune 1's patterns: notes (a note number then a length index) and commands ($FE and a number), to $C6C0. $C60A-$C65D is a pattern no order list names.
